Hi all — quick privacy counsel read-through and recommendations:
- Subprocessors: push to provide a current inventory and a 30-day notice plus opt-out on specified high-risk subprocessor additions. Customer asking for affirmative consent is negotiable; recommend: notice + cure period rather than prior consent.
- Transfers: accept SCCs + Redwood EU Addendum; customer redline that mandates a particular mechanism is OK if we can match to our standard addendum. We should not accept language that prevents fallback mechanisms (e.g., our internal regional model endpoints).
- Audit/SOC: decline unlimited on-demand on-site audits. Offer SOC 2 Type II report and a limited right to audit via third-party assessor once per 12 months for production-affecting issues.
- Liability: push back on removing regulatory fine caps; offer carveout language limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct.

I've prepared a marked-up doc (Redline_ThermoWave_DPA_marked.docx) with line-level proposals and comments. Key negotiation points for sales to highlight in the next call: retention buckets (30/90/365), anonymization definition, and subprocessor notice cadence.

Marcus Lin
